arXiv:1411.4921v4 [quant-ph] 02 Jun 2016

Quantum Conditional Mutual Information, Reconstructed States, and State Redistribution

Fernando G.S.L. Brandão1,5, Aram W. Harrow2, Jonathan Oppenheim3, Sergii Strelchuk4 Affiliation: 1 Department of Computer Science, University College London, Gower St, London WC1E 6BT, UK
2 Center for Theoretical Physics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge MA 02139, USA
3 Department of Physics, University College London, Gower St, London WC1E 6BT, UK
4 Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics, University of Cambridge, Wilberforce Road, Cambridge CB3 0WA, UK 5Quantum Architectures and Computation Group, Microsoft Research, Redmond, WA 98052-6399, USA
Abstract

We give two strengthenings of an inequality for the quantum conditional mutual information of a tripartite quantum state recently proved by Fawzi and Renner, connecting it with the ability to reconstruct the state from its bipartite reductions. Namely, we show that the conditional mutual information is an upper bound on the regularized relative entropy distance between the quantum state and its reconstructed version. It is also an upper bound for the measured relative entropy distance of the state to its reconstructed version. The main ingredient of the proof is the fact that the conditional mutual information is the optimal quantum communication rate in the task of state redistribution.

Quantum information theory is the successful framework describing the transmission and storage of information. It not only generalized all of the classical information-theoretic results but also developed a wealth of tools to analyze a number of scenarios beyond the reach of the latter, such as entanglement processing. One of the central quantities of the classical information theory that directly generalizes to quantum information is the conditional mutual information (CMI). For a tripartite state ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} it is defined as

I​(C:R|B)ρ\displaystyle I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho} (1)
:⁣=\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}= S​(B​C)ρ+S​(B​R)ρ−S​(B​C​R)ρ−S​(B)ρ,\displaystyle S(BC)_{\rho}+S(BR)_{\rho}-S(BCR)_{\rho}-S(B)_{\rho},

with S​(X)ρ:=−tr⁡(ρX​log⁡ρX)S(X)_{\rho}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=-\tr(\rho_{X}\log\rho_{X}) as von Neumann entropy. It measures the correlations of subsystems CC and RR relative to subsystem BB. The fact the classical CMI is non-negative is a simple consequence of the properties of the probability distributions; the same fact for the quantum CMI is equivalent to a deep result of quantum information theory – strong subadditivity of the von Neumann entropy [1]. Naturally, this led to a variety of applications in different areas, ranging from quantum information theory [4, 3, 2] to condensed matter physics [7, 5, 6].

In the classical case, for every tripartite probability distribution pX​Y​Zp_{XYZ},

I(X:Z|Y)=minq∈MCS(p||q),I(X\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}Z|Y)=\min_{q\in\text{MC}}S(p||q), (2)

where S(p||q):=∑ipilog(pi/qi)S(p||q)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sum_{i}p_{i}\log(p_{i}/q_{i}) is the relative entropy and the minimum is taken over the set MC of all distributions qq such that X−Y−ZX-Y-Z form a Markov chain. Equivalently, the minimization in the right-hand side of Eq. (2) could be taken over Λ⊗idZ⁡(pY​Z)\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{Z}(p_{YZ}), for reconstruction channels Λ:Y→Y​X\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}Y\rightarrow YX. In particular, I⁡(X:Z|Y)=0I(X\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}Z|Y)=0 if, and only if, X−Y−ZX-Y-Z form a Markov chain (which is equivalent to the existence of a channel Λ:Y→Y​X\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}Y\rightarrow YX such that pX​Y​Z=Λ⊗idZ⁡(pY​Z)p_{XYZ}=\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{Z}(p_{YZ})).

The class of tripartite quantum states ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} satisfying I​(C:R|B)ρ=0I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho}=0 has also been similarly characterized [8]: The BB subsystem can be decomposed as B=⨁kBL,k⊗BR,kB=\bigoplus_{k}B_{L,k}\otimes B_{R,k} (with orthogonal vector spaces BL,k⊗BR,kB_{L,k}\otimes B_{R,k}) and the state written as

ρB​C​R=⨁kpk​ρC​BL,k⊗ρBR,k​R\rho_{BCR}=\bigoplus_{k}p_{k}\rho_{CB_{L,k}}\otimes\rho_{B_{R,k}R} (3)

for a probability distribution {pk}\{p_{k}\} and states ρC​BL,k∈C⊗BL,k\rho_{CB_{L,k}}\in C\otimes B_{L,k} and ρBR,k​R∈BR,k⊗R\rho_{B_{R,k}R}\in B_{R,k}\otimes R. States of this form are called quantum Markov because in analogy to Markov chains, conditioned on the outcome of the measurement onto {BL,k⊗BR,k}\{B_{L,k}\otimes B_{R,k}\}, the resulting state on CC and RR is product.

Paralleling the classical case, ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} is a quantum Markov state if, and only if, there exists a reconstruction channel Λ:B→B​C\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC such that Λ⊗idR⁡(ρB​R)=ρB​C​R\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})=\rho_{BCR} 11 1 Ref. [8] shows that Markov states have perfect reconstruction maps; see Eq. (19) for an explicit formula. The converse is straightforward. If Λ⊗idR⁡(ρB​R)=ρB​C​R\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})=\rho_{BCR} then Λ⁡(ρB)=ρB​C\Lambda(\rho_{B})=\rho_{BC}. Using the recovery condition, and the monotonicity of relative entropy under applying first (Λ⊗idR)(\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}) and then trC\tr_{C}, we obtain S(ρB​C​R∥ρR⊗ρB​C)=S((Λ⊗idR)ρB​R∥(Λ⊗idR)(ρB⊗ρR))≤S(ρB​R∥ρB⊗ρR)≤S(ρB​C​R∥ρB​C⊗ρR).S(\rho_{BCR}\|\rho_{R}\otimes\rho_{BC})=S((\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R})\rho_{BR}\|(\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R})(\rho_{B}\otimes\rho_{R}))\leq S(\rho_{BR}\|\rho_{B}\otimes\rho_{R})\leq S(\rho_{BCR}\|\rho_{BC}\otimes\rho_{R}). It then follows that I(C:R|B)=S(ρB​C​R∥ρB​C⊗ρR)−S(ρB​R∥ρB⊗ρR)=0I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)=S(\rho_{BCR}\|\rho_{BC}\otimes\rho_{R})-S(\rho_{BR}\|\rho_{B}\otimes\rho_{R})=0.. Having generalized the definition of CMI, can we also retain the above equivalence, with the set of quantum Markov states taking the role of Markov chains? Surprisingly, it turns out that this is not the case [9] and it seems not to be possible to connect states that are close to Markov states with states of small conditional mutual information in a meaningful way (see, however, [2, 10]).

Nonetheless, it might be possible to relate states with small conditional mutual information with those that can be approximately reconstructed from their bipartite reductions, i.e. such that Λ⊗idR⁡(ρB​R)≈ρB​C​R\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})\approx\rho_{BCR}. Indeed, several conjectures appeared recently in this respect [5, 14, 12, 13].

A recent breakthrough result from Fawzi and Renner gives the first such connection. They proved the following inequality [15]:

I(C:R|B)ρ≥minΛ:B→B​CS1/2(ρB​C​R||Λ⊗idR(ρB​R))I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho}\geq\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC}S_{1/2}(\rho_{BCR}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})) (4)

with S1/2(ρ||σ):=−2logF(ρ,σ)S_{1/2}(\rho||\sigma)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=-2\log F(\rho,\sigma) the order-1/21/2 Rényi relative entropy, where F⁡(ρ,σ)=tr⁡[(σ12​ρ​σ12)12]F(\rho,\sigma)=\tr[(\sigma^{\frac{1}{2}}\rho\sigma^{\frac{1}{2}})^{\frac{1}{2}}] is the fidelity [17]. It implies that if the conditional mutual information of ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} is small, there exists a reconstructing channel Λ:B→B​C\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC such that Λ⊗idR⁡(ρB​R)\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR}) has high fidelity with ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR}.

In this Letter, we prove a strengthened version of the Fawzi-Renner inequality. We also give a simpler proof of the inequality based on the task of state redistribution, [4] which gives an operational interpretation to the conditional mutual information.

Result. Let S(ρ||σ):=tr[ρ(logρ−logσ)]S(\rho||\sigma)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\tr[\rho(\log\rho-\log\sigma)] be the quantum relative entropy of ρ\rho and σ\sigma. Define the measured relative entropy as

𝕄S(ρ||σ)=maxM∈ℳS(M(ρ)||M(σ)),\mathbb{M}S(\rho||\sigma)=\max_{M\in{\cal M}}S(M(\rho)||M(\sigma)), (5)

where ℳ{\cal M} is the set of all quantum-classical channels M(ρ)=∑ktr(Mkρ)|k⟩⟨k|M(\rho)=\sum_{k}\tr(M_{k}\rho)\left|k\right\rangle\left\langle k\right|, with {Mk}\{M_{k}\} a POVM and {|k⟩}\{\left|k\right\rangle\} an orthonormal basis.

The main result of this Letter is the following:

Theorem 1.

For every state ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR},

I​(C:R|B)ρ\displaystyle I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho} (6a)
≥\displaystyle\geq limn→∞minΛn:Bn→Bn​Cn1nS(ρB​C​R⊗n||Λn⊗idRn(ρB​R⊗n))\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\Lambda_{n}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n}}\frac{1}{n}S(\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n}||\Lambda_{n}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R^{n}}(\rho_{BR}^{\otimes n})) (6b)
≥\displaystyle\geq minΛ:B→B​C𝕄S(ρB​C​R||Λ⊗idR(ρB​R))\displaystyle\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC}\mathbb{M}S(\rho_{BCR}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})) (6c)
≥\displaystyle\geq minΛ:B→B​CS1/2(ρB​C​R∥Λ⊗idR(ρB​R)).\displaystyle\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC}S_{1/2}(\rho_{BCR}\|\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})). (6d)

Eq. (6d) is the Fawzi-Renner inequality (Eq. (4)) and follows from Eq. (6c) using the bound S(π||σ)≥S1/2(π||σ)S(\pi||\sigma)\geq S_{1/2}(\pi||\sigma) [18] and the fact that minM∈ℳ⁡F⁡(M⁡(π),M⁡(σ))=F⁡(π,σ)\min_{M\in{\cal M}}F(M(\pi),M(\sigma))=F(\pi,\sigma) [19]. Eq. (6c) also generalizes one side of Eq. (2) to quantum states, implying that it is optimal at least for classical states ρ\rho.

Our lower bound provides a substantial improvement over the original Fawzi-Renner bound even for classical states. To see this, consider the classically correlated state ρC​B​R=ρC​R⊗𝕀BdB\rho_{CBR}=\rho_{CR}\otimes{\frac{\mathbb{I}_{B}}{d_{B}}} with d:=dC=dRd\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=d_{C}=d_{R} and ρC​R=(1−ϵ)​|00⟩​⟨00|C​R+ϵd−1​∑k=1d−1|k​k⟩​⟨k​k|C​R\rho_{CR}=(1-\epsilon)|00\rangle\langle 00|_{CR}+\frac{\epsilon}{d-1}\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}|kk\rangle\langle kk|_{CR}. Then Eq. (6c) becomes 𝕄S(ρB​C​R||σB​C⊗ρR)\mathbb{M}S(\rho_{BCR}||\sigma_{BC}\otimes\rho_{R}), where σB​C\sigma_{BC} depends on the channel Λ\Lambda that minimizes Eq. (6c). The measured relative entropy is equal to the ordinary classical relative entropy between the distribution pB​pC​Rp_{B}p_{CR} (generated from ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR}) and the product distribution qB​C​pRq_{BC}p_{R} (generated from σB​C⊗ρR\sigma_{BC}\otimes\rho_{R}) optimized over all quantum-classical channels. Observing that pC​Rp_{CR} is maximally correlated whereas qC​pBq_{C}p_{B} is the product distribution irrespective of Λ\Lambda, Eq. (6c) equals to I⁡(C:R)≈ϵ​log⁡(d−1)I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R)\approx\epsilon\log{\left(d-1\right)}. The corresponding Fawzi-Renner bound (6d) becomes −log⁡F⁡(ρC​R,ρC⊗ρR)≤−log⁡(1−ϵ)≈ϵ-\log F(\rho_{CR},\rho_{C}\otimes\rho_{R})\leq-\log(1-\epsilon)\approx\epsilon. Thus, the lower bound (6c) is optimal for classical states.

Another application of our result is the well-known problem of classification of the short-range entangled states studied by Kitaev [16]. Defining such a class of states is nontrivial and one of the natural properties to be required is the ability generate them locally: There must exist a O⁡(1)O(1) quantum circuit that generates the designated state from a product state. In particular, one sees that states with low conditional mutual information can be generated from the product states according to the Fawzi-Renner bound. Our result improves the lower bound when we quantify the distance between the states using measured relative entropy.

Li and Winter conjectured in [10] that Eq. (6c) could be strengthened to have the relative entropy in the right-hand side (instead of the measured relative entropy). We leave this as an open question, but we note that Eq. (6b) shows that an asymptotic version of the conjectured inequality does hold true.

Proof of Theorem 1: The main tool in the proof will be the state redistribution protocol of Devetak and Yard [4, 24, 23] which gives an operational meaning for the conditional mutual information as twice the optimal quantum communication cost of the protocol. Consider the state |ψ⟩A​B​C​R⊗n\left|\psi\right\rangle_{ABCR}^{\otimes n} shared by two parties (Alice and Bob) and the environment (or reference system). Alice has An​CnA^{n}C^{n} (where we denote nn copies of AA by AnA^{n} and likewise for CC,BB and RR), Bob has BnB^{n}, and RnR^{n} is the reference system. In state redistribution, Alice wants to redistribute the CnC^{n} subsystem to Bob using preshared entanglement and quantum communication.

It was shown in [4, 24] that using preshared entanglement Alice can send the CnC^{n} part of her state to Bob, transmitting approximately (n/2)​I​(C:R|B)(n/2)I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B) qubits in the limit of a large number of copies nn. More precisely:

Lemma 2 (State Redistribution Protocol [4, 24]).

For every |ψ⟩A​B​C​R\left|\psi\right\rangle_{ABCR} there exist completely positive trace-preserving encoding maps ℰn:An​Cn​Xn→An​Gn\mathcal{E}_{n}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}A^{n}C^{n}X_{n}\rightarrow A^{n}G_{n} and decoding maps 𝒟n:Bn​Gn​Yn→Bn​Cn\mathcal{D}_{n}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}G_{n}Y_{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n} such that

limn→∞∥𝒟n∘ℰn(|ψ⟩⟨ψ|A​B​C​R⊗n⊗ΦXn​Yn)−|ψ⟩⟨ψ|A​B​C​R⊗n∥1=0\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|\mathcal{D}_{n}\circ\mathcal{E}_{n}(\left|\psi\right\rangle\left\langle\psi\right|_{ABCR}^{\otimes n}\otimes\Phi_{X_{n}Y_{n}})-\left|\psi\right\rangle\left\langle\psi\right|_{ABCR}^{\otimes n}\|_{1}=0 (7)

and

limn→∞logdim(Gn)n=12​I​(C:R|B)ρ,\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\log\dim(G_{n})}{n}=\frac{1}{2}I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho}, (8)

where ρB​C​R:=trA(|ψ⟩⟨ψ|A​B​C​R)\rho_{BCR}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\tr_{A}(\left|\psi\right\rangle\left\langle\psi\right|_{ABCR}) and ΦXn​Yn\Phi_{X_{n}Y_{n}} is a maximally entangled state shared by Alice (who has XnX_{n}) and Bob (who has YnY_{n}), and ∥.∥1\|.\|_{1} denotes the trace norm.

We split the proof of Theorem 1 into the proof of Proposition 3 and Eq. (17) below.

Proposition 3 follows from the state redistribution protocol outlined above. The main idea is the following: Suppose that in the state redistribution protocol Bob does not receive any quantum communication from Alice, but instead he ”mocks” the communication (locally preparing the maximally mixed state in GnG_{n}) and applies the decoding map 𝒟n\mathcal{D}_{n}. It will follow that even though the output state might be very far from the target one, the relative entropy per copy of the output state and the original one cannot be larger than twice the amount of communication of the protocol (which is given by the conditional mutual information).

Proposition 3.

For every state ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR},

I​(C:R|B)ρ\displaystyle I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)_{\rho} (9)
≥\displaystyle\geq limn→∞minΛ:Bn→Bn​Cn1nS(ρB​C​R⊗n||Λ⊗idRn(ρB​R⊗n)).\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n}}\frac{1}{n}S(\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R^{n}}(\rho_{BR}^{\otimes n})).
Proof.

Let ϕGn​Yn​An​Bn​Rn:=ℰn⊗idBn​Rn​Yn(|ψ⟩⟨ψ|A​B​C​R⊗n⊗ΦXn​Yn)\phi_{G_{n}Y_{n}A^{n}B^{n}R^{n}}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\mathcal{E}_{n}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{B^{n}R^{n}Y_{n}}(\left|\psi\right\rangle\left\langle\psi\right|_{ABCR}^{\otimes n}\otimes\Phi_{X_{n}Y_{n}}) be the state after the encoding operation.

minσ∈QMSS(ρB​C​R||σB​C​R)\displaystyle\min_{\sigma\in\text{QMS}}S(\rho_{BCR}||\sigma_{BCR}) (18)
≥\displaystyle\geq I(C:R|B)≥minΛ:B→B​R𝕄S(ρB​C​R||Λ⊗idR(ρB​R)),\displaystyle I(C\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}R|B)\geq\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BR}\mathbb{M}S(\rho_{BCR}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})),

with QMS the set of quantum Markov states given by Eq. (3). For probability distributions the lower and upper bounds in Eq. (18) coincide, giving Eq. (2). However, in the quantum case, the two can be very far from each other.

An interesting question is whether we can also have equality in the quantum case when minimizing over the set of reconstructed states. In particular we can ask whether Eq. (9) holds with equality. It turns out that this is false and can be disproved using pure states of dimension 2×2×22\times 2\times 2 and the transpose channel, defined for a tripartite state ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} as

T(π):=ρB​C(ρB−1/2πρB−1/2⊗idC)ρB​C.T(\pi)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sqrt{\rho_{BC}}\left({\rho_{B}^{-1/2}}\pi{\rho_{B}^{-1/2}}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{C}\right)\sqrt{\rho_{BC}}. (19)

In Fig. 1 we plot the conditional mutual information against the reconstructed relative entropy using the transpose channel (i.e. S(ρB​C​R∥TB⊗idR(ρB​R))S(\rho_{BCR}\|T_{B}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR}))) for 10,000 randomly chosen pure states of dimension 2×2×22\times 2\times 2. We see that for roughly 73% of the points, the relative entropy is strictly smaller than the conditional mutual information when using the transpose channel. Since any particular reconstruction map also puts an upper bound on the minimum relative entropy, Eq. (9) must sometimes be a strict inequality. Similar numerical results were found in an unpublished early version of [10].

In the proof of Theorem 1 we were not able to give an explicit optimal reconstruction map. In the context of approximate recovery for pure states, the transpose channel is optimal up to a square factor [20] (using the fidelity as a figure of merit). We could ask whether the same holds for mixed states.

Another interesting open problem is whether we can improve the lower bound in Eq. (18) to have the relative entropy, instead of the measured relative entropy. Proposition 3 and Lemma 8 in the Supplemental Material show that the result would follow from the following conjectured inequality: Given a state ρ\rho, a convex closed set of states 𝒮{\cal S}, and a measure μ\mu with support only on 𝒮{\cal S},

lim infn→∞1nS(ρ⊗n||∫μ(dσ)σ⊗n)≥?minσ∈𝒮S(ρ||σ).\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}S\left(\rho^{\otimes n}||\int\mu(d\sigma)\sigma^{\otimes n}\right)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle?}}{{\geq}}\min_{\sigma\in{\cal S}}S(\rho||\sigma). (20)

The case when ρB​R=ρB⊗ρR\rho_{BR}=\rho_{B}\otimes\rho_{R} was recently proven in [22]. We can also easily prove the inequality classically, using hypothesis testing, which is universal for the alternative hypothesis. However, since there is no quantum hypothesis test universal for the alternative hypothesis [21] for general sets 𝒮{\cal S}, we leave the inequality in the quantum case as an open problem for future work.

.2 The measured entropy lower bound

To prove the inequality stated in the Eq. (17) of the main text, we first prove the following lemma which is a version of the postselection technique of [29] for quantum operations.

Lemma 8.

For every permutation-invariant quantum operation Λ:Bn→Bn​Cn\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n} and every state π∈Bn\pi\in B^{n},

Λ⁡(π)≤poly⁡(n)​∫ℰ⊗n​(π)​μ​(𝑑ℰ),\Lambda(\pi)\leq\poly(n)\int{\cal E}^{\otimes n}(\pi)\mu(d{\cal E}), (32)

where μ\mu is a measure over quantum operations ℰ:B→B​C{\cal E}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC.

Proof.

Since Λ:Bn→Bn​Cn\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n} is permutation-invariant, it follows that its Jamiolkowski state JΛ∈𝒟⁡((B¯n⊗Bn⊗Cn)CLOSEJ_{\Lambda}\in{\cal D}((\overline{B}^{n}\otimes B^{n}\otimes C^{n}) (with B¯≅B\overline{B}\cong B) is permutation-invariant. We now apply Lemma 7 in the Supplemental Material to find a distribution μ\mu over σ∈𝒟⁡(B¯⊗B⊗C)\sigma\in\mathcal{D}(\overline{B}\otimes B\otimes C) with

JΛ≤poly⁡(n)​∫σ⊗n​μ​(𝑑σ),J_{\Lambda}\leq\poly(n)\int\sigma^{\otimes n}\mu(d\sigma), (33)

and each σB¯=τB¯\sigma_{\bar{B}}=\tau_{\bar{B}}. This latter condition means that each σ\sigma can be also thought of as JℰJ_{\mathcal{E}} for some ℰ:B→B​C\mathcal{E}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC. We complete the proof using the relation:

trB¯n⁡((πT⊗IBn​Cn)​JΛ)\displaystyle\tr_{\overline{B}^{n}}((\pi^{T}\otimes I_{B^{n}C^{n}})J_{\Lambda}) (34)
≤\displaystyle\leq poly⁡(n)​∫trB¯n⁡((πT⊗IBn​Cn)​Jℰ⊗n)​μ​(𝑑ℰ),\displaystyle\poly(n)\int\tr_{\overline{B}^{n}}((\pi^{T}\otimes I_{B^{n}C^{n}})J_{{\cal E}}^{\otimes n})\mu(d{\cal E}),

and the fact that trB¯n⁡((πT⊗IBn​Cn)​JΛ)=Λ⁡(π)/dim​(B)n\tr_{\overline{B}^{n}}((\pi^{T}\otimes I_{B^{n}C^{n}})J_{\Lambda})=\Lambda(\pi)/\text{dim}(B)^{n} and trB¯n⁡((πT⊗IBn​Cn)​Jℰ⊗n)=ℰ⊗n​(π)/dim​(B)n\tr_{\overline{B}^{n}}((\pi^{T}\otimes I_{B^{n}C^{n}})J_{{\cal E}}^{\otimes n})={\cal E}^{\otimes n}(\pi)/\text{dim}(B)^{n}.   ⊓\sqcap⊔\sqcup

We now turn to proving the measured entropy lower bound:

Proposition 9 (Eq. (17) in the main text).

For every state ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} one has

limn→∞minΛ:Bn→Bn​Cn1nS(ρB​C​R⊗n||Λ⊗idRn(ρB​R⊗n))\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n}}\frac{1}{n}S(\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R^{n}}(\rho_{BR}^{\otimes n})) (35)
≥\displaystyle\geq minΛ:B→B​C𝕄S(ρB​C​R||Λ⊗idR(ρB​R)).\displaystyle\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC}\mathbb{M}S(\rho_{BCR}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR})).

Lemma 8 gives that for every Λn:Bn→Bn​Cn∈\Lambda_{n}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n}\in Sym,

with μ⁡(d​ℰ)\mu(d{\cal E}) a measure over quantum operations ℰ:B→B​C{\cal E}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC. Using the previous equation and the operator monotonicity of the log\log (see Lemma 4 above),

limn→∞minΛ:Bn→Bn​Cn1nS(ρB​C​R⊗n||Λ⊗idRn(ρB​R⊗n))\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\Lambda\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B^{n}\rightarrow B^{n}C^{n}}\frac{1}{n}S(\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n}||\Lambda\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R^{n}}(\rho_{BR}^{\otimes n})) (38)
≥\displaystyle\geq limn→∞minμn1nS(ρB​C​R⊗n∥∫(ℰ⊗idR(ρB​R))⊗nμn(dℰ)).\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\mu_{n}}\frac{1}{n}S\left(\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n}\hskip 2.84544pt\|\int({\cal E}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R}(\rho_{BR}))^{\otimes n}\mu_{n}(d{\cal E})\right).

To complete the proof we make use of Lemma 6 above. Consider the state ρB​C​R⊗n\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n} and let XX be the first copy of ρB​C​R\rho_{BCR} in the tensor product and YY the remaining ρB​C​R⊗n−1\rho_{BCR}^{\otimes n-1}. Define

K=⋃k∈ℕ(conv{(ℰ⊗idR)(ρB​R)⊗k:ℰ:B→BC}),K=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\left(\text{conv}\{({\cal E}\otimes{\operatorname{id}}_{R})(\rho_{BR})^{\otimes k}\hskip 2.84544pt\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\hskip 2.84544pt{\cal E}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B\rightarrow BC\}\right), (39)

i.e. the convex hull of tensor products of reconstructed states. It is easy to check that KK satisfies the assumption of Lemma 6 above. Therefore:
